extracted.intended_audience: Recording Academy Voting Members, GRAMMY entrants (artists, producers, engineers, songwriters), Chapter representatives, and their publicists/teams
extracted.subtask_description: Official Recording Academy rules governing nominating committees, voting conduct, For Your Consideration (FYC) communications, nomination corrections/challenges, limits on nominations, and which roles receive statuettes vs certificates in GRAMMY Categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional and National Craft Nominating Committee nomination process
rubrics_metrics.description: For specified Categories (e.g., Producer of the Year, Classical; Engineered Album, Classical; Contemporary Classical Composition) the first round is by General Voting Membership; the second round occurs in National Craft Nominating Committees. The top 50 selections from General Voting Membership in each Category appear on the ballot for the National Craft Nominating Committees to vote by confidential ballot to select the five nominations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each Regional Craft Nominating Committee (Eastern, Western, Southern) has 15 Voting Members from Chapters in their regions. National committee comprised of ~40–50 members; Classical Producers committee includes Engineers and Engineering committee includes Producers. For many craft categories, Regional Committees receive a list of no less than 50 titles (more if ties) from first round membership voting to consider and confidentially ballot to select five nominations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional craft committee voting for Recording Package & Boxed/Special/Limited-Edition Package
rubrics_metrics.description: Recording Package and Boxed/Special/Limited-Edition Package are judged in Regional Craft Nominating Committees where members view and judge entries and vote by confidential ballot to select five nominations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This regional process is similar to other craft categories but does not involve a General Voting Membership first ballot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Album Notes remote national committee procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Best Album Notes is voted by a single National Craft Nominating Committee that does not meet in person; 30–50 Voting Members access a password-protected Academy website to view all Notes entries and vote via a return envelope sent directly to the independent auditing firm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Votes are tabulated by the independent firm to determine the five nominations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immersive Audio Album committee eligibility and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominations for Best Immersive Audio Album are selected by a committee of 20–25 Voting Members who must be Voting Members in good dues standing and meet certain qualifications in the Engineering or Producing fields and be approved by the Trustees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee reviews all Immersive Audio Album entries in their meeting and votes for the final five nominees in the Category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft committee member selection and population
rubrics_metrics.description: Committees are populated similarly to current Craft Committees, with names proposed from Chapters and Wings (e.g., Songwriters & Composers Wing for Composition committee; Producers & Engineers Wing for Producer & Engineering committee members).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Recording Academy compiles and vets names; final appointments follow Academy policy and relevant approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee service terms and turnover
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee Members serve five years on and one year off; Committee Chairs serve three years on and two years off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Goal of 25% turnover each year by the fourth year. No committee member may serve more than five consecutive years without a one-year break. A member selected as Chair may serve up to an additional three years before taking two years off if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Songwriter of the Year Nominating Committee process
rubrics_metrics.description: Regional Songwriter Of The Year Nominating Committees are comprised of diverse and 'highly relevant' songwriters assembled by the Recording Academy from Chapter suggestions vetted by Awards Department, CEO and Recording Academy Chair. Nominating Committees meet once and are given a list of voters' top 30 choices in alphabetical order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committees receive submitted material (audio and lyrics) for listed songwriters, discuss, and at the end submit secret weighted ballots of their top five selections; ballots tallied determine final nominees. Committee chairs are recommended by secret ballot at the end of the meeting. Committee chairs guide the process and must be impartial though they are Voting Members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chair role and impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chair's job is to guide the committee through the process and to remain impartial on committee decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chair is a Voting Member and serves in conjunction with an Academy Staff member. Chair recommendations for the following year are made by committee secret ballot in accordance with Academy policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline for claiming a nomination before telecast
rubrics_metrics.description: A deadline is established for those not credited appropriately in liner notes or metadata to claim nominee status: two weeks after the announcement of the nominations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To seek correction, the potential recipient must inform the Awards Department specifying inaccurate or omitted submissions, explain why the error occurred, and state steps taken to correct it. The Academy may require further documentation. Once reviewed and approved by the head of Awards, the correction is made. Any individual claiming a nomination after the deadline will be notified that official changes will be made after the awards telecast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process for corrections to nominations
rubrics_metrics.description: Correction requests must detail what was inaccurately submitted or omitted, explain why the error happened, and describe corrective steps; Awards Department may request further documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approved corrections are made by the head of Awards. Corrections after the two-week deadline are deferred until after the telecast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenges to GRAMMY Award entitlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions regarding GRAMMY Award entitlement are made by the Awards Department. Any challenge to a final entitlement decision must be made in writing and addressed to the Executive Committee of the Recording Academy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Executive Committee can investigate, consider and decide the challenge and is empowered to act with the power of the Board of Trustees for that purpose. Its decision is communicated in writing to the challenger and shall be final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of nominations any nominee may receive (Rules A–F)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall policy on how many nominations an individual nominee (Artist, Producer, Conductor, etc.) may receive in a given year is governed by Rules A–F with specified exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule A: 1 nomination only. Rule B: No limit on number of nominations. Rule C: 1 nomination to the Artist — exceptions: 2 nominations if the 2nd is with a co-nominee OR 2 nominations if each are with a different co-nominee. Rule D: 1 nomination per music video or music film. Rule E: 1 nomination — exception: 2 nominations if the Artist is different. For Classical: 1 nomination — exception: 2 nominations if orchestra or co-nominee is different; 2 nominations for choral conductor if chorus is different. Rule F: 2 nominations permitted as follows: 1 individual nomination and 1 co-nomination; 2 individual nominations; or 2 co-nominations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category-specific nomination-rule assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Category is assigned which of Rules A–F applies (denoted by letters next to Categories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document lists many Categories mapping to Rule letters (e.g., Record Of The Year (C); Album Of The Year (C); Song Of The Year (B); Best New Artist (A); many genre and craft Categories annotated with (A), (B), (C), (D), (E), or (F)). Additional footnotes specify Rule exceptions depending on whether the nominee is an Artist, Producer, Conductor, etc. (e.g., '* Rule C if Artist is nominee; *Rule B if Producer is nominee; *Rule A if Artist is nominee; *Rule E if Conductor is nominee and orchestra is different').

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserving integrity: general enforcement and corrective actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Academy's goal is that the Awards process is fair and ethical and that Voting Members base choices solely on artistic and technical merits. Activities contrary to guidelines may lead to corrective actions including disqualification of entries and suspension/termination of membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Academy may take corrective actions for activities deemed to undermine the letter or spirit of Academy regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voter code of conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Voters shall not allow their choices to be suggested, directed or influenced by anything other than their own analysis of merit, including personal friendships, company loyalties, regional preferences, or sales volume/popularity. Voters shall not accept money or anything of value in exchange for votes, access to members, submission of materials, or any membership privilege.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voters must not enter into agreements or understandings on how to vote, including forming 'Voting Blocs' or engaging in 'Vote Trading'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on bloc voting and related corrective authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Voting Blocs and vote trading are explicitly prohibited (groups agreeing to vote together, or offering votes in exchange).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Academy reserves the right to set guidelines for its independent accountants to take confidential corrective action as they deem appropriate if bloc voting or other coordinated solicitation is detected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final voting secrecy and tabulation
rubrics_metrics.description: After nominations announcement, the final ballot is made available to all current Voting Members to select GRAMMY winners. All ballots, including special committees, are tabulated confidentially by an independent accounting firm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results remain unknown until the GRAMMY Awards when Deloitte delivers sealed envelopes with winners' names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescindment policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The GRAMMY process does not produce a ranked result. If a GRAMMY Award is withdrawn following the presentation, no award is given in that Category for that year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No alternate or runner-up is awarded in the same year if an award is rescinded post-presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: For Your Consideration (FYC) proprietary-information policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbers specific to official awards Category, Field and/or balloting, entry lists and finals lists are proprietary to the Recording Academy and may not be used, disclosed, published, or distributed in connection with any event, advertisement or other purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if tactics are not specifically prohibited elsewhere, they should not be assumed acceptable; Academy will review materials or answer questions in advance if requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: FYC communications — permitted content
rubrics_metrics.description: FYC marketing communications (emails, mailings, invitations, social media, websites, print ads) are permitted only if they include an opt-out option and are limited to promoting only the sender's own recordings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted elements include: artwork related to product; brief, unembellished descriptions of the recording or creators; copies or links to product; links to websites promoting eligible recordings; link to Recording Academy website with guidelines; lists of creators who worked on the recording; reference to nominations once announced (Category names by full name); and reference to the GRAMMY Award by name using proper registered marks (GRAMMY®, GRAMMY® Award, GRAMMY Awards® (plural), GRAMMYs®). Use of the logo is prohibited (reserved for paid sponsors/partners).

rubrics_metrics.name: FYC communications — prohibited content and practices
rubrics_metrics.description: FYC communications cannot cast negative or derogatory light on competing recordings, exaggerate merits, include Recording Academy trademarks/logos or protected information, include entry or Category numbers, include chart numbers/streams/sales/RIAA awards, include personal signatures/personal pleas to listen, misrepresent past/present honors, or reference the year/telecast number (e.g., '2022' or '65th GRAMMY Awards').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members and publicists may promote only their own recordings; no lobbying on behalf of other members. The Academy does not disclose member contact information; exercise caution with vendors claiming accurate member lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hosting and attending FYC events — hospitality and ticket rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent FYC events may be hosted if they adhere to guidelines; FYC activities may not include complimentary meals, alcoholic beverages, gifts, or any hospitality that could be inferred as value in exchange for votes. Ticketed FYC events require members to purchase tickets at full price; no comps or discounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Widespread gifting of show tickets to members as part of an explicit or implicit FYC/vote solicitation campaign is not allowed; Chapters may not be used as a conduit for gifting. Tickets not acquired by members through personal affiliations must be purchased at full price. Academy-hosted events may not receive FYC product mailings (such mailings will be disposed of or returned).

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone lobbying prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: Contacting Academy members by phone to promote a GRAMMY-eligible product or achievement is prohibited, even if framed as confirming product receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phone solicitation for promotion or vote solicitation is not allowed under any circumstances described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party solicitation by independent contractors is forbidden
rubrics_metrics.description: No marketing companies have authorized access to Recording Academy member lists or staff. Vendors claiming to have such lists are false; entries that used such vendors will be disqualified if the vendor obtained the lists through wrongful conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a vendor obtained an accurate member list through wrongful conduct, any entry that used that vendor’s services may be disqualified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording Academy FYC website feature rules
rubrics_metrics.description: RecordingAcademy.com offers For Your Consideration promotional listings free of cost for official entries during the first round voting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members whose releases are official entries may post a link or upload their entry once in each approved FYC Category (once per accepted Category). Duplicate posts, posts in wrong Category (miscategorized), and promoting entries outside For Your Consideration groups are violations; content will be removed and repeated violations may result in penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording Academy membership-hosted activities restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: GRaMMY-submitted product cannot be the topic of any Recording Academy Voting Member activity or promotion at Academy-hosted events, social media, recorded/streaming content, or any context where it may be perceived as the Academy promoting an eligible product to Voting Members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Talent not submitting product in the current cycle may participate fully in Academy activities. Once product is submitted, FYC product distribution at Academy-hosted events is prohibited; violators will be asked to leave and may be subject to additional penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting violations contact and enforcement posture
rubrics_metrics.description: The Academy encourages community reporting of guideline violations and provides contact information: 877.637.6816 / awards@recordingacademy.com.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Academy is willing to review questionable tactics in advance and will investigate reported findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards, certificates and crediting rules (statuette vs certificate)
rubrics_metrics.description: The document specifies, by Category, which roles receive a GRAMMY statuette and which receive a Winners Certificate, with thresholds such as >50% playing time determining statuette recipients and lesser contributions receiving Certificates. Special rules apply in certain Categories (e.g., Music For Visual Media, Score Soundtrack for Video Games where composer percentage thresholds apply).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and key thresholds: Record Of The Year statuette: Artist & Producer, Engineer/Mixer, Mastering Engineer (if other than Artist). Album Of The Year statuette: Artist(s) including Featured Artists, Songwriters of new material, Producers, Recording Engineers, Mixer(s) & Mastering Engineer(s). For many album Categories, those credited with >50% playing time receive statuette; those with <50% receive Certificates. For Score Soundtrack For Video Games & other interactive media, a minimum of 33% playing time is required for composer credit rules; if composers have separate production teams the 33% applies to teams, with certificates possible for those under thresholds. The page enumerates this allocation for dozens of Categories (pop, rock, R&B, rap, country, jazz, classical, production, composing/arranging, package/notes/historical, etc.) and includes role-specific notes (e.g., for Musical Theater Album, up to 3 Producers for new recordings, up to 2 Music Supervisors, engineer/mixer thresholds, special rules for ensemble-driven pieces). Refer to the Category mapping on the page for the full per-Category role assignments and certificate/statuette distinctions.
